ideas.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ideas.thesis: NVDA appeared in all 6 of 6 overnight screens with unanimous high conviction — the strongest signal in today's digest. The stock trades ~39% below the consensus analyst price target of $302.83 (current ~$217) while guiding ~95% YoY revenue growth for the upcoming quarter, yet carries roughly the same forward multiple as the S&P 500 (21x). With the August 26 earnings report 14 days away and BofA explicitly flagging a beat-and-raise, a defined-risk call spread (Sep/Oct expiry) is the preferred structure to capture the pre-earnings run while limiting binary print exposure in an elevated IV environment.
ideas.catalyst: Q2 FY2027 earnings report — August 26, 2026 after close; BofA expects beat-and-raise on $500B AI infrastructure capex cycle
ideas.edge: Consensus analyst target $302.83 vs. last ~$217.55 = ~39% upside gap; 58 of 61 analysts rate Buy/Strong Buy; BofA $350 target implies ~61% upside; stock trades at 21.1x forward earnings despite ~95% guided YoY revenue growth
ideas.bull_case: A beat-and-raise print on Aug 26 re-rates the stock toward consensus targets, with AI infrastructure capex commitments providing multi-year revenue visibility; call spreads allow participation with capped downside before the binary event.
ideas.bear_case: Elevated IV makes options expensive, and any guidance miss or macro hawkish shock from today's CPI could compress tech multiples further; post-earnings IV crush could hurt long options even on a moderate beat.

ideas.name: SK Hynix Inc. (ADR)
ideas.thesis: SKHY appeared in all 6 of 6 overnight screens and represents the most extreme fundamental-vs-price dislocation in today's digest. The stock has fallen ~30% from its July peak on geopolitical/risk-off sentiment while posting record Q2 results: 76% operating margins and +257% YoY revenue growth — figures that are fundamentally inconsistent with a ~$135–143 price vs. a consensus analyst target of $245.46 (+70–82% upside). The HBM4 production ramp is confirmed for H2 2026, and Cantor Fitzgerald issued a 12-month double call on August 4. The selloff appears sentiment-driven, not fundamental, making this a high-conviction mean-reversion candidate with a staged or options-based entry near $155 Fibonacci resistance.
ideas.catalyst: HBM4 mass production ramp H2 2026; Cantor Fitzgerald 12-month double call issued Aug 4, 2026; potential China plant stake sale decision pending
ideas.edge: Consensus analyst target $245.46 vs. current ~$135–143 = ~70–82% upside gap; forward P/E of 5.19x on 76% operating margins; stock -30% from July peak on geopolitical noise, not earnings deterioration
ideas.bull_case: Record margins and HBM4 ramp are intact — as geopolitical sentiment normalizes, the stock re-rates sharply toward $155 near-term resistance and eventually toward the $245 consensus target; Amazon AI commitment through 2028 validates long-duration demand.
ideas.bear_case: Broken short-term technicals (lower highs and lows) signal continued distribution; geopolitical risk (China tensions, export controls) could escalate and impair the HBM4 ramp or force asset sales at unfavorable terms.

ideas.name: Invesco QQQ Trust (Nasdaq-100 ETF)
ideas.thesis: QQQ appeared in 4 of 6 overnight screens as the preferred vehicle to express today's CPI binary via defined-risk options. The 10-year yield sits at 4.7%, the Nasdaq was already -0.6% Tuesday, and September Fed hike probability is ~55% — creating an asymmetric setup where a hot CPI print (consensus 3.4% YoY core) compresses tech multiples further, while a soft print matching BofA's 2.5% YoY forecast could catalyze a sharp relief rally. Short-dated weekly or August-expiry options (straddle or directional spread) are the recommended structure rather than outright index exposure.
ideas.catalyst: July CPI print — today August 12 at 8:30 AM ET; FOMC September 15–16 decision, with hike probability near 55%
ideas.edge: BofA forecasts core CPI at 2.5% YoY (lowest since January) — a soft print directly removes September hike risk and is an unambiguous bullish catalyst for tech-heavy QQQ; elevated IV into CPI creates cheap defined-risk structures in either direction
ideas.bull_case: A soft CPI print eases September hike fears, yields pull back from 4.7%, and QQQ bounces sharply — a call spread or straddle captures the relief rally with limited capital at risk.
ideas.bear_case: Energy-driven CPI surprise to the upside reprices September hike odds toward certainty, pushing the 10-year higher and compressing Nasdaq multiples; put spreads or the short leg of a straddle benefit in this scenario.

ideas.name: SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust
ideas.thesis: SPY appeared in 2 of 6 overnight screens — the minimum qualifying threshold — as a complementary macro hedge to QQQ. ideas.catalyst: July CPI print — today August 12 at 8:30 AM ET; September FOMC rate decision Sep 15–16, 2026 (~50-55% hike probability)
ideas.edge: VIX at 15.28 (suppressed) with 10Y yield at 4.696% and June CPI at 3.5% YoY; energy +21% MoM creates upside CPI risk — put spreads are historically cheap at this vol level relative to the macro binary risk
ideas.bull_case: A soft CPI print resolves the Fed uncertainty in the market's favor, yields decline, and SPY resumes its uptrend — the hedge expires worthless but portfolio longs benefit.
ideas.bear_case: An upside CPI surprise resurrects September hike conviction, compresses P/E multiples across the S&P, and SPY put spreads pay out with high convexity given how little hedging is currently in place.
